processing: Hand-picked buds of the Yunnan large-leaf variety are oxidised as black tea and rolled by hand into small coils.
harvest_season: Not fixed by any standard; pure-bud lots depend on spring and other flushes that give plump buds, and spring is usually the most prized, as with other Dian Hong.
appearance_dry: Small, tight golden snails of pure bud, fuzzy to the touch.
appearance_wet: Plump, soft buds of golden copper, slowly uncoiling.
taste_profile: Sweet honey and a smooth texture, with a light fruity aroma and a long, pleasant finish.

brewing.notes: Makers suggest near-boiling water and a heaped teaspoon per 250 to 300 ml for 3 to 5 minutes in a mug. Gongfu with short steeps and slightly cooler water is more forgiving for pure bud.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year, like most fine Dian Hong, and best within a couple of years while the honey aroma is lively. Sellers often distinguish pure-bud lots from one-bud-one-leaf versions, so check which you are buying.
description:
Jin Luo means golden snail, and one look explains it: small coils of pure golden bud. It is a kind of Dian Hong, Yunnan's black tea family, and one of the easiest to recognise on a table.

The buds come from the same large-leaf variety used for much of Yunnan's pu-erh. They are picked by hand and rolled by hand into coils. Being all bud, the coils stay golden rather than turning black. The tea is linked with Simao in Pu'er.

The cup is amber, sweet with honey, smooth, with a light fruitiness and a long finish. Pure bud can go sharp if pushed, so short steeps are safer. If a long steep has gone astringent, pouring it off into a second vessel promptly is the fix.

Look for even, whole coils. 'King' grades are a marketing tier without a shared standard, so judge by the leaf. A close cousin, Bi Luo Chun Hong Cha, may include leaf as well as bud.
history:
Little is documented about the origins of this particular shape, and no firm date or maker is on record. It belongs to the wider Dian Hong line.

The tea has become well known abroad under English names such as Golden Snail and Yunnan Pure Bud Golden Snail, and Russian-speaking shops also sell it as Red Dragon or Red Spiral.
